title: Jesus' Miracles IQ
subtitle: How well do you know the signs and wonders of Jesus?

questions.text: What was Jesus' first miracle, according to John?

options.text: Healing a blind man
options.explanation: Jesus healed the blind on several occasions, but that was not His first sign.

options.text: Turning water into wine at a wedding
options.explanation: At a wedding in Cana, Jesus turned water into wine, the first of His signs (John 2:11).

options.text: Calming a storm
options.explanation: Calming the storm came later in His ministry, not as the first sign.

options.text: Feeding the five thousand
options.explanation: The feeding of the crowd was a famous miracle, but it came after the wedding at Cana.

questions.text: How did Jesus feed the large crowd of five thousand?

options.text: With five loaves and two fish
options.explanation: Jesus took five loaves and two fish, gave thanks, and fed them all (Matthew 14:17-21).

options.text: With bread that fell from the sky
options.explanation: Manna fell in Moses' day. Jesus multiplied a boy's small lunch instead.

options.text: With seven baskets of grain
options.explanation: He started with five loaves and two fish. The leftovers filled twelve baskets.

options.text: With fish caught from the sea
options.explanation: He did not send the disciples fishing. He multiplied the loaves and fish already there.

questions.text: What did Jesus do during the storm on the Sea of Galilee?

options.text: He steered the boat to shore
options.explanation: Jesus did not row to safety. He spoke to the storm itself.

options.text: He calmed the wind and the waves with a word
options.explanation: Jesus rebuked the wind and said, "Peace, be still," and the sea grew calm (Mark 4:39).

options.text: He told the disciples to swim
options.explanation: No one had to swim. Jesus stilled the storm with a command.

options.text: He prayed until the storm passed on its own
options.explanation: The sea did not calm on its own. Jesus rebuked it directly and it obeyed.

questions.text: Which friend of Jesus did He raise after he had been dead four days?

options.text: Lazarus
options.explanation: Jesus called Lazarus out of the tomb after four days, and he came out alive (John 11:43-44).

options.text: Nicodemus
options.explanation: Nicodemus came to Jesus by night with questions, but he was not raised from the dead.

options.text: Zacchaeus
options.explanation: Zacchaeus was the tax collector who climbed a tree to see Jesus, not the man raised from death.

options.text: Bartimaeus
options.explanation: Bartimaeus was a blind man Jesus healed, not the friend raised after four days.

questions.text: What did Jesus do that astonished the disciples one night out on the lake?

options.text: He walked on the water
options.explanation: Jesus came to them walking on the sea, and Peter briefly walked toward Him (Matthew 14:25-29).

options.text: He turned the lake to dry land
options.explanation: The lake stayed water. The wonder was that Jesus walked on top of it.

options.text: He made the boat fly
options.explanation: The boat did not fly. Jesus Himself walked across the water to the disciples.

options.text: He filled the lake with light
options.explanation: There was no glowing lake. Jesus simply walked on the surface of the water.

questions.text: How did Jesus heal a man who had been blind from birth, according to John 9?

options.text: He made clay and put it on the man's eyes
options.explanation: Jesus made clay with spit, anointed his eyes, and told him to wash in a pool (John 9:6-7).

options.text: He gave the man new glasses
options.explanation: There were no glasses in that day. Jesus used clay and a washing in the pool.

options.text: He simply walked past him
options.explanation: Jesus did more than pass by. He made clay and sent the man to wash and see.

options.text: He prayed over the man for seven days
options.explanation: There was no week of waiting. The man washed once and came back seeing.

questions.text: What did Jesus tell the paralyzed man to do after healing him?

options.text: Take up his bed and walk
options.explanation: Jesus said, "Arise, take up thy bed, and walk," and the man got up at once (John 5:8).

options.text: Stay in bed and rest
options.explanation: Jesus did the opposite. He told the man to pick up his mat and walk.

options.text: Wait for the pool to stir
options.explanation: The man had waited by the pool for years. Jesus healed him without it.

options.text: Go and find a doctor
options.explanation: He needed no doctor after this. Jesus told him to rise and carry his bed.

questions.text: What happened when a woman touched the edge of Jesus' garment in the crowd?

options.text: She was healed of a long illness
options.explanation: She had bled for twelve years, and at His touch she was made whole (Mark 5:25-29).

options.text: Nothing happened to her
options.explanation: Something did happen. She was healed the moment she touched His garment.

options.text: She fainted from the crowd
options.explanation: She did not faint. Her years-long illness was healed instantly.

options.text: She was scolded and sent away
options.explanation: Jesus did not send her away. He called her 'daughter' and affirmed her faith.

questions.text: How many men with leprosy did Jesus heal at once in Luke 17, and how many came back to thank Him?

options.text: Ten were healed, and one returned to thank Him
options.explanation: Ten lepers were cleansed, but only one, a Samaritan, came back to give thanks (Luke 17:12-19).

options.text: Five were healed, and all five returned
options.explanation: There were ten, and sadly only one of them came back to say thank you.

options.text: Twelve were healed, and none returned
options.explanation: It was ten men, and one did return to thank Jesus.

options.text: Three were healed, and two returned
options.explanation: The number was ten healed, with just one grateful man coming back.

questions.text: Whose daughter did Jesus raise from death, telling her to arise?

options.text: Jairus, a ruler of the synagogue
options.explanation: Jairus begged Jesus to come, and Jesus raised his young daughter (Mark 5:22-42).

options.text: Pilate, the governor
options.explanation: Pilate was the Roman governor at Jesus' trial, not the father of this girl.

options.text: Herod, the king
options.explanation: Herod ruled the region, but it was Jairus whose daughter Jesus raised.

options.text: Caiaphas, the high priest
options.explanation: Caiaphas was the high priest who opposed Jesus, not the girl's father.

questions.text: What is the greatest miracle at the center of the Gospel message?

options.text: Jesus rising from the dead
options.explanation: On the third day Jesus rose. As the angel said, "He is not here, for he is risen" (Matthew 28:6, ASV).

options.text: Jesus feeding the four thousand
options.explanation: That feeding was a real miracle, but the resurrection is the heart of the good news.

options.text: Jesus cursing a fig tree
options.explanation: The fig tree was a sign with a lesson, but the resurrection is the central miracle.

options.text: Jesus paying tax with a coin from a fish
options.explanation: That was a small wonder of provision. The resurrection stands at the center of it all.

scoring.perfectMessage: You know the wonders of Jesus by heart.

gradeBands.label: Onlooker
gradeBands.message: A great prompt to read the Gospels and watch the miracles unfold.

gradeBands.label: Witness
gradeBands.message: You know many of the signs Jesus did.

gradeBands.label: Believer
gradeBands.message: You know the miracles of Jesus very well.

gradeBands.label: Marvel
gradeBands.message: Amazing. The signs and wonders of Jesus are clearly familiar ground.
